back: When the demand for foreign currency (imports, debts, other payments) exceeds the supply available to the country.
The stock of foreign currency held by the central bank (the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe) to pay for imports and support the currency.

front: Give five causes of foreign currency shortages.
back: Low export earnings (drought, falling prices); high import demand; debt repayments; profits sent abroad; capital flight; illegal outflows; overvalued official rate.

front: Give five problems caused by foreign currency shortages.
back: Shortages of fuel and medicines; factory closures and job losses; inflation; parallel markets; debt problems; lower investment.

front: Name six sources of foreign currency for Zimbabwe.
back: Mineral exports; farm exports (tobacco); tourism; remittances; foreign direct investment; loans and grants; processed exports to the region.
An unofficial market for foreign currency, usually at a rate above the official one, which appears when official supplies are short.

front: Why is borrowing not a lasting solution to a foreign currency shortage?
back: Loans must be repaid with interest, adding to future outflows of foreign currency.

front: Long-run solution to foreign currency shortages?
back: Raise and diversify earnings: value-added and varied exports, tourism, attracting investment and remittances through official channels.
